brief.headline: Push for a 10–12% price cut in exchange for faster payment — they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% peer, and their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d, so they'll value quicker payment.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–12% price cut, paid back through faster payment
priceAsk.target: A cut worth roughly their borrowing rate of 12.19%, funded by paying them 15 days faster
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% of every sale vs 3.8% at similar firms — there's room in their price. Market asking prices for 28 mm PP caps (₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95) are MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume. Their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at peers, so paying them faster is worth about 12.19% (what they pay to borrow money).

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (15 days instead of 30) in return for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹22.57 L of our cash, which we trade for the price cut

brief.financialLeverage: They're healthy — rated CRISIL A+ / Stable, profitable (keep 5.9% vs 3.8% peer), and growing fast (22.1%/yr). But their cash is stuck longer than most (104d vs 79d), so they need cash flow. We're only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — tiny customer — so we can't lean on volume threat alone. The play is to offer faster payment (worth 12.19% to them) in exchange for a matching price cut. Their strong finances mean we can push firmly without risking supply.

evidence.point: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% at similar firms — room in their price
Their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at peers — they need cash flow
They borrow money at 12.19% — paying them faster is worth that rate
They already pay their own suppliers slower than most — 49d vs 37d — so asking for more payment time is fair
We're only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — we're a small customer
Market asking price for 28 mm PP caps: ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Health score B (65/100). Top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr) — pails, containers, pharma packaging. Health score B (73/100). Strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer, India-Pan presence, medium confidence. Not yet audited or priced.

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue — too small to threaten walking away alone. Build credibility by naming the two alternates (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) and showing we've qualified second sources.
They're in the grey zone (Altman Z 2.17) — not distressed, but not bulletproof. Don't squeeze so hard that cash flow tips them over; frame the faster payment as a partnership move, not a squeeze.

Market asking prices are already MARKET-FAIR (₹0.85–0.95 typical) — the 10–12% cut relies on swapping payment speed and volume commitment, not just benchmarking. If they refuse, fall back to a smaller cut (5–6%) and keep 30-day terms.
They're growing fast (22.1%/yr) and rated A+ — they have options. Lead with the cash-flow benefit of faster payment, not a hard price ultimatum.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help free up your cash — we'll pay you 15 days faster if you can cut our price by 10–12%, roughly what faster payment is worth to you.
